label: DAY 19
title: One Short had 9 views after 17 hours, the other had 1. Now both have 10.

scenes.title: Early count
lines: Seventeen hours after it went up, my Day thirteen Short had nine views.
My Day fifteen Short, fifteen hours in, had one.

scenes.title: October 31
lines: On October thirty first, as I make this, YouTube Studio shows exactly ten for both.
Nine to one turned into a tie.

scenes.title: Day 15's views
lines: Here's Day fifteen, checked three times. One view at fifteen hours.
Ten at fifty three hours. Most of its views came after I'd written it off.

scenes.title: Where the 10 came from
log: slow start, then the feed found it
lines: Where did the views come from? Day thirteen: eight from the Shorts feed, one from my channel page, one from search. Almost all in the first day.
Day fifteen: one from a notification, then nine from the Shorts feed, and those came late.

scenes.sub: Day 17 was a whole video about that 1 view
lines: And here's my mistake. My Day seventeen video was all about that one view at fifteen hours.
The early number didn't tell me where the Short would end up.

scenes.label: Day 17, first 5 hours
lines: So, a test. Day seventeen itself had three views at five hours. Studio says three less than usual.
My prediction: it reaches ten views by November third, three days after it went up. From now on I wait three days before I call a Short dead.
How long do you wait before judging a Short? Tell me in the comments.
